items.headline: Bitcoin holds near $84k over the weekend, no fresh catalyst
items.summary: Bitcoin was trading around $83,900-84,000 as of Saturday morning SGT (24h range roughly $83,230-$85,208), consolidating below Monday's intraweek high near $87,300. Ethereum held near $2,690, essentially flat over the weekend with no distinct new catalyst since Friday's close.
items.actionable: Crypto is quiet and rangebound this weekend -- no signal to change stance; it remains a secondary risk-sentiment gauge rather than a driver right now.

items.headline: Wall Street closes hawkish week with a rally as 10-year yield hits post-2008 high
items.summary: The S&P 500 rose 0.51% to 7,743.41, the Dow gained 0.93% to 51,828.62 (snapping a three-week losing streak), and the Nasdaq added ~0.48% to 27,068.72 on Friday, with all three posting weekly gains despite the 10-year Treasury yield climbing to 5.18%, its highest since the 2008 financial crisis. VIX eased to ~14.9 even as the bond selloff continued.
items.actionable: Equities shrugging off 5%+ yields is a near-term risk-on tell, but the yield/vol divergence still favors keeping the cash pile large rather than chasing the rally.

items.headline: Iran hands US a 4-5 day ultimatum on Hormuz reopening terms
items.summary: Iranian Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei said Tehran gave Washington 'four or five days' to fully accept its written roadmap -- a regionwide ceasefire of up to 60 days, a phased Hormuz reopening, and an end to the US naval blockade -- delivered to US envoys during a three-hour UN session. Rezaei said Iran will not reopen the strait unless the US acts first, with a new front around the Red Sea/Bab al-Mandab possible if talks fail.
items.actionable: The ultimatum clock (expiring roughly Mon-Tue 28-29 Sep) is the key weekend-into-week catalyst for oil and therefore for silver/gold-miner beta -- watch for escalation risk overriding the truce-hope rally that's been capping crude.

items.headline: Houthis strike Saudi Aramco's Yanbu hub and a Riyadh target; six missiles intercepted
items.summary: Yemen's Houthis claimed missile and drone strikes on a target in Riyadh and Aramco facilities at the Red Sea port of Yanbu on 25 September; the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted six ballistic missiles, with no confirmed damage or casualties. Aramco supplies roughly 10% of global oil demand; analysts said Brent is unlikely to fall much below $100 while the conflict continues.
items.actionable: Continued Houthi strikes on Saudi infrastructure alongside the Hormuz ultimatum keep the oil-shock/inflation-hedge case for gold-silver miners intact even as Friday's tape pulled back -- don't read the daily pullback as thesis-breaking.

items.headline: Oil eases from Thursday spike as truce hopes offset Houthi risk premium
items.summary: Brent crude fell to roughly $105.3/barrel (-1.2%) and WTI to roughly $92.7/barrel (-2%) on Friday, retreating from Thursday's intraday high above $108 after reports that US and Iranian negotiators were exploring a phased Hormuz-reopening deal. The Brent-WTI spread widened to $12.68, the largest since May, partly on fears of a potential US diesel export ban.
items.actionable: Oil remains elevated (Brent above $100) despite the Friday pullback, so the inflation/real-yield headwind pressuring gold and silver this week is more a dollar/real-yield story than an oil-demand-destruction one -- keep miner exposure sized for continued volatility around the Iran deadline.

items.headline: Gold and silver pull back on stronger dollar and higher real yields
items.summary: Gold closed around $4,265/oz (down roughly 0.5-0.6%) and silver around $63.5/oz (down roughly 1.1-1.4%) on Friday as a firmer US dollar and rising real yields (10-year nominal at 5.18%) outweighed safe-haven demand. Analysts characterized the move as a macro-driven pullback, not a reversal -- a turn in the dollar or real yields, or a fresh geopolitical shock, could quickly restore upward pressure.
items.actionable: This is the key near-term risk for the levered silver/gold-miner book: rising real yields are the dominant headwind right now, not falling geopolitical risk -- a further leg up in the 10Y toward/through 5.2-5.3% would likely pressure GDX/SILJ/SLVP further even if the war premium in oil holds.

items.headline: BofA Flow Show: global equity funds swing to outflow as US leads the reversal
items.summary: BofA's weekly Flow Show (week ended 23 Sep 2026) showed US equity funds losing $21.1bn and global equity funds losing a net $10.2bn -- a sharp reversal from the prior week's +$63.8bn US equity inflow (the best week in three months). Fixed income kept its 74-week inflow streak alive (+$17.3bn); the Bull & Bear Indicator eased to 9.3, still in the contrarian 'Sell' zone.
items.actionable: A one-week swing from the best equity-inflow week in three months to an outright outflow, arriving right as the 10-year hit a post-2008 high, is an early tell that the hawkish-Fed repricing is starting to bite fund positioning -- a reason not to read Friday's index rally as confirmation the flow backdrop has turned durably risk-on.

items.headline: Consumer sentiment slides to four-month low on fuel prices and tariffs
items.summary: University of Michigan consumer sentiment fell to a four-month low on Friday, driven by elevated pump prices and lingering tariff concerns, even as headline equity indices rallied -- a growing wedge between resilient risk assets and weakening household-level data.
items.actionable: Weakening consumer data alongside a hawkish Fed strengthens the case for staying defensive/cash-heavy rather than adding domestic-consumer-exposed risk.

items.headline: US-China critical-minerals talks end without a concrete deal; magnet flows still 'not up to par'
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Bessent and USTR Greer met Vice Premier He Lifeng in New York the week of 21 September for preparatory talks covering AI safety guardrails, the tariff-truce extension, and rare-earth magnet flows, concluding around Trump-Xi's 24 September Washington meeting with no public outcome or new deadline announced. A senior US official said China's mineral-flow restoration has underperformed expectations, consistent with the 21% month-on-month drop in Chinese rare-earth magnet exports to the US in August (to 512 tons).
items.actionable: Persistently constrained Chinese magnet exports with no resolution from this week's talks keeps the structural bull case for the rare-earth watchlist (MP Materials, Lynas, USA Rare Earth) intact; JL Mag (6680.HK) is more exposed to any China-side demand slowdown given its onshore position.

items.headline: Trump and Xi hold Washington summit, agree to hold trade truce status quo
items.summary: President Trump concluded meetings with President Xi Jinping in Washington on 24 September, with both sides agreeing to maintain the existing trade-truce terms (extended to mid-January 2027) for several more months rather than escalate, and announcing plans for a joint AI-safety summit in Shenzhen this November. The meeting produced no new concessions on rare-earth export flows.
items.actionable: A truce-preserving (not truce-deepening) summit outcome argues for a neutral-to-cautious stance on HK tech beta -- the downside tail (renewed tariff escalation) is reduced but the upside catalyst (a rare-earth flow resolution) didn't materialize either.

items.headline: Hang Seng slips 1% in thin trade as tech and property drag
items.summary: The Hang Seng Index closed down 1.01% at 24,510.09 and the Hang Seng Tech Index fell 1.13% to 4,311.78 on Friday, with Xiaomi (-2.6%), NetEase (-3.1%) and other tech names lower and Chinese property developers also weighing on the index. Sentiment showed little lift from the week's Trump-Xi meeting, with a senior US official separately saying China's rare-earth magnet flow restoration 'has not been up to par.'
items.actionable: Weak follow-through in HK tech despite the Trump-Xi truce extension argues for staying selective in 0700/0981/1810 rather than adding broad beta into thin holiday liquidity; watch for a bounce if critical-minerals friction eases.

items.headline: Suntec REIT to sell three Australian offices, sharpen Singapore focus
items.summary: Suntec REIT will launch formal sale campaigns for three freehold Grade-A offices in Australia -- 177 Pacific Highway and 21 Harris Street in Sydney, and its 50%-owned 477 Collins Street in Melbourne -- following a post-sponsor-change strategic review. Management said successful divestment would cut aggregate leverage to below 40%, easing the earnings drag from high Australian rates and freeing capacity for buybacks, distributions, or Singapore-focused acquisitions.
items.actionable: A credible deleveraging and portfolio-simplification path is a positive read-through for the SGX REIT book generally -- Suntec's move to below-40% leverage removes one overhang that's been weighing on S-REIT valuations amid the high-rate backdrop.

items.headline: Jefferies initiates Singapore banks: Buy DBS and UOB, Hold OCBC
items.summary: Jefferies started coverage citing the banks' proven resilience across credit cycles, superior capital generation, and further scope for earnings/dividend compounding, with OCBC initiated at Hold (the lowest rating of the three). The call comes as rising SORA following the Fed hike is seen restoring net interest margins after years of compression.
items.actionable: Fresh sell-side conviction on DBS/UOB reinforces the case that the Singapore bank leg of the book is the direct beneficiary of the same hawkish Fed pivot that is hurting the silver/gold miners leg -- a natural internal hedge within the portfolio.

note: Weekend catch-up run, Saturday 26 Sep 2026 07:02 SGT. Markets are closed over the weekend; the latest completed sessions are Fri 25 Sep (US/HK/SG cash equities) and Thu 24 Sep (JPX). Active alternate 2026 macro backdrop remains 'Hawkish-Fed war-shock': the Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 16 Sep under new Chair Kevin Warsh, and the 10-year Treasury yield pushed to 5.18% on Friday, its highest since 2008, even as the S&P 500 rallied 0.51% into the weekly close. Iran issued a fresh 4-5 day ultimatum on Hormuz reopening on 24 Sep (expiring roughly Mon-Tue 28-29 Sep) -- the key catalyst to watch heading into next week. 4 items above (26/25/25/25 Sep) are within the last 24-48h, satisfying the freshness requirement; crypto was checked explicitly since it trades through the weekend and is quiet/rangebound with no new catalyst.
